name: neural-office-static-html-review-v1
authorship: Synthetic cases and literal expected findings authored by the reviewing agent before running this corpus. audit_html was not used to generate expectations. The reviewer read the implementation to identify the declared scope; this is not a blind or held-out evaluation.
purpose: A deterministic no-model baseline for four heuristic families, plus explicit semantic probes that can expose omissions.
encoding: UTF-8 by default; line and column are one-based Unicode character positions. Global document findings use line 1, column 1.
limitations: Twenty selected synthetic cases do not estimate real-world precision, recall or user utility.
A matching result is not WCAG conformance, browser rendering, accessible-name computation or a security audit.
No model commentary is generated or scored; this corpus cannot establish a winning model or agent count.
Heuristic presence checks do not establish that language, image alternatives or labels are appropriate.
Semantic probes retain the desired manual expectation even when the current checker cannot meet it. They are not counted as passing heuristic cases.

cases.purpose: Zero input: distinguish a missing document root from missing title text.
cases.rationale: There is no literal html element and no title text. This is a full-document heuristic, not an HTML fragment validator.

cases.purpose: Negative control: a named, language-declared document with no images or controls.
cases.rationale: All applicable presence checks are satisfied; no assertion is made about the rest of accessibility.

cases.purpose: Positive control with one finding from each heuristic family and independent source positions.
cases.rationale: Whitespace does not provide title text. Neither image alternative nor control name is present.

cases.purpose: Declare the full-document boundary when the source contains only a fragment.
cases.rationale: The heuristic requires a literal html element. Browsers may infer elements and HTML permits some tag omission; this finding is not a claim that a fragment is invalid or inaccessible.

cases.purpose: Whitespace and character references must not masquerade as meaningful title or language values.
cases.rationale: Both values are whitespace-only. Ordering is by source position and then code.

cases.purpose: Image presence check with an author-declared informative use.
cases.rationale: The image has no alt attribute. The checker does not interpret pixels or synthesize a correct alternative.

cases.purpose: Negative control: an explicitly decorative image uses an empty alternative.
cases.rationale: Empty alt is intentional for the decorative role stated by the case author. This does not imply empty alt is suitable for informative images.

cases.purpose: Order independence: the matching explicit label may follow its control.
cases.rationale: The label for value exactly matches the control id and supplies text even though it appears later.

cases.purpose: Negative control for a nonempty wrapping label.
cases.rationale: The checkbox is nested in the label that describes its purpose.

cases.purpose: An unrelated label must not suppress a candidate for another control.
cases.rationale: The for/id values differ; there is no alternate naming attribute.

cases.purpose: Exercise input, select and textarea independently with ordered findings.
cases.rationale: An option value and textarea content are not the label of their enclosing control.

cases.purpose: Negative controls for nonempty aria-label, a real aria-labelledby target and title fallback.
cases.rationale: These are candidates for naming in the declared heuristic. Title alone is not asserted to be a good visible-label design.

cases.purpose: Document exclusions for hidden and action input types without claiming they need no accessibility review.
cases.html:
<html lang="es">
<head><title>Acciones</title></head>
<body>
  <input type="hidden" value="synthetic">
  <input type="submit" value="Enviar">
  <input type="reset" value="Restablecer">
  <input type="button" value="Vista previa">
  <input type="image" src="send.png" alt="Enviar">
</body></html>
cases.rationale: The control-label candidate check excludes these input types. The image input supplies its own alt; image-input semantics are outside the img-only heuristic.

cases.purpose: Do not scan commented markup or a script string as if they were elements in the document.
cases.rationale: The parser should treat these regions as inert source content. No browser or script runtime is invoked by this test.

cases.purpose: BOM, CRLF, uppercase HTML and multibyte characters preserve readable one-based source coordinates.
cases.rationale: The img begins after two spaces and two Unicode characters. Column is not a UTF-8 byte offset.

cases.purpose: Whitespace-only naming attributes cannot suppress a missing-label candidate.
cases.rationale: No nonempty naming value, label association or label ancestor exists.

cases.purpose: An inapplicable type attribute must not suppress review of an unnamed select.
cases.rationale: Select has no type content attribute that makes it a hidden input. Adding this irrelevant attribute should not remove the candidate seen for the ordinary unnamed select.

cases.purpose: An inapplicable input-style type must not suppress review of an unnamed textarea.
cases.rationale: The textarea remains a multiline text control; the unrelated type attribute does not supply a label or change it to an action input.

semantic_probes.purpose: An unresolved IDREF should not count as a demonstrated accessible name.
semantic_probes.rationale: No element has the referenced id, and no other naming source is supplied. This tests a semantic gap beyond attribute presence; it does not require claiming a full accessible-name algorithm.

semantic_probes.purpose: Association alone does not establish a nonempty control name.
semantic_probes.rationale: The associated label has no text, descendants or alternative name and there is no other naming source. Detecting this requires more than matching for/id.
